etymology.historical_story: The English turning verb veer is traced to French virer, meaning to turn. English additionally has a historically separate nautical verb concerning letting out rope, so identical spelling does not guarantee a single origin. Neither history establishes a Malay borrowing. Malay uses Vietnam as a complete foreign place name; its historical components are not Malay prefixes or suffixes. etymology.historical_story: J. K. Rowling invented Voldemort as a name with French associations: vol can suggest flight or theft, while mort means death. Within the story, Tom Marvolo Riddle rearranges his name into “I am Lord Voldemort,” creating a grander identity. These associations connect the name with his obsession with death; they are not Malay word formation. See [the official account](https://www.harrypotter.com/features/the-different-meanings-behind-lord-voldemorts-many-names).

etymology.historical_story: Nama vodka berasal daripada bahasa Rusia, dengan hubungan kepada voda yang bermaksud air dan bentuk pengecil yang lazim diterangkan sebagai air kecil. Nama lembut ini merujuk kepada minuman keras, bukannya air biasa. Dalam bahasa Melayu, vodka diterima sebagai satu kata pinjaman utuh; unsur Rusia di dalamnya tidak menjadi imbuhan Melayu. Sumber: [Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/vodka).

etymology.historical_story: Viking belongs to a historical naming tradition connected with Old Norse seafaring and raiding. The deeper origin of the term remains debated, so the familiar explanation that it simply means a person from a bay should not be treated as settled fact. Modern historical usage also includes trading voyages and overseas settlement. [Australian National Maritime Museum](https://www.sea.museum/en/learn/resource/vikings).

etymology.historical_story: Vicky is an English familiar form of Victoria. Victoria comes from the Latin word for victory and was also the name of the Roman goddess of victory. The shorter form illustrates how personal names develop affectionate everyday alternatives. In Malay conversation, Vicky functions as a person’s name rather than as a translation of victory. [Sources: Vicky](https://www.behindthename.com/name/vicky), [Victoria](https://www.behindthename.com/name/victoria).
